text: You've seen the graphical plan, and you've seen the numbers from STATISTICS TIME and IO. Today, two more ways to capture a plan — one old, one modern.

SET STATISTICS PROFILE ON is the older option — before SSMS could draw a graphical plan tree, this is how you got operator details: an extra result set of plain rows and columns, estimated versus actual row counts, cost per operator. It still works, but Microsoft has marked it deprecated. Kept around for old scripts, not something to build new habits around.

SET STATISTICS XML ON does something the graphical Ctrl+M plan can't: it returns the actual plan as an XML value, right in your results grid, alongside your normal query results. Click that XML link, and SSMS opens the exact same graphical tree you already know — except now it's also data.

And because it's data, you can save it. Run your query, click the XML result, save it as a dot sqlplan file — a portable snapshot of exactly what SQL Server did. Make your index change, capture another one. Now you've got a real before-and-after record you can double-click open anytime, without ever re-running the original query.

A graphical plan in the moment is great — but it disappears the second you close that tab. Capturing it as XML makes it permanent. Next lesson: temp tables, table variables, and CTEs — not just the syntax, but which one actually performs better and when. See you there.
